Feature Grid as Radiance Field represents a 3D scene by decomposing the high-dimensional radiance field tensor into low-rank components (vectors and matrices), significantly reducing memory usage compared to dense voxel grids [S1, S3].

The claim states that 'Feature Grid as Radiance Field' represents a 3D scene by decomposing high-dimensional radiance field tensors into low-rank components (vectors and matrices) to reduce memory usage compared to dense voxel grids. Source [S3] explicitly describes a method (EgoNeRF) that uses explicit feature grids for density and appearance, decomposes these feature tensors into vectors and matrices via low-rank tensor factorization, and states that this reduces space complexity from O(n^3) to O(n^2). Source [S1] describes TensoRF, which also expands on voxel-based techniques by factoring 3D voxel grids into low-rank tensor components to significantly reduce memory consumption. Both sources support the core mechanism (tensor decomposition into low-rank components) and the benefit (reduced memory/space complexity compared to dense storage) described in the claim.
